sections.title: Hedging: saying less than you could
sections.content: When you are not sure, or do not want to sound too direct, you hedge: you soften a claim. You already have several tools. You know *se dice que* and *al parecer* from B2 Unit 18, *por lo visto*, *tal vez* and *seguramente* from B2 Unit 3, and *me parece que* from B1 Unit 7. This lesson adds four more: *parece que* + indicative, *según parece*, the conditional *podría decirse que*, and *tal vez convendría* for a gentle suggestion.

sections.title: Four ways to soften
rows: Parece que el plan no funciona.
It seems the plan is not working. (an impression)
Según parece, la reunión empieza a las tres.
Apparently the meeting starts at three. (as far as one can tell)
Podría decirse que el plan no funciona del todo.
One could say the plan does not entirely work. (a possibility, not a fact)
Tal vez convendría revisar el horario.
Perhaps it would be a good idea to check the schedule. (a suggestion)

items.spanish: Parece que va a llover toda la tarde.
items.english: It looks like it will rain all afternoon.

items.spanish: Según parece, el director no puede venir hoy.
items.english: Apparently the director cannot come today.

items.spanish: Podría decirse que fue un buen año para la empresa.
items.english: One could say it was a good year for the company.

items.spanish: Tal vez convendría hablar con la jefa antes de decidir.
items.english: Perhaps it would be a good idea to talk to the boss before deciding.

sections.content: Compare: *El plan no funciona* (blunt), *Parece que el plan no funciona* (an impression), *Podría decirse que el plan no funciona del todo* (very careful). One hedge is enough: more than one sounds heavy. Affirmative *parece que* takes the indicative; *no parece que* takes the subjunctive, as *no creo que* does (B1 Unit 7): *No parece que sea fácil*.
